sections.heading: YIN: A New Dawn for Yogic Traditions
paragraphs: A 200-hour Yin yoga teacher training goes far beyond learning long-held poses. Students study functional anatomy, fascia, skeletal variation, Yin–Yang philosophy, Traditional Chinese Medicine, meridian theory, safe sequencing, prop use, contraindications and teaching methodology. The training helps future teachers understand why a posture is selected, which area it targets and how it should be adapted for different bodies. If you want to know more about our Yin yoga course dates and curriculum, or you want to join our Yin yoga teacher training course in Bali, visit the course page for all details.

sections.heading: Understanding the Yin Yoga teacher training curriculum (Detailed)
paragraphs: The Yin yoga teaching curriculum spans from one week to a 200-hour intensive immersion, typically including subjects like Yin & Yang yoga asanas, Traditional Chinese Medicine Philosophy, Anatomy, Alignment workshops and Meditation. The Yin yoga teacher training syllabus is extended through live classroom sessions, coursebooks or manuals along with documentaries, case studies and audio-visual resources.

subsections.heading: Yin Yoga Anatomy
paragraphs: Detailed study of the Spine and the Hip joint along with deeper understanding of Joints and Connective tissues. Fascia – a connective tissue deeper in the layers of the skin – improves cellular function, reception and repair. The focus of Yin yoga is to bring about gentle stimulation for fascia and hydrating the connective tissues. Functional anatomy for Yin yoga helps students understand systemic anatomical effects of practice and engagement of smaller joints and muscles.

subsections.heading: Philosophy of TCM and Yin Yoga
paragraphs: The Philosophy of TCM includes a basic understanding of Yoga Philosophy, Daoist Philosophy, the principles of conducting life inspired by Buddhism, and ancient therapeutic practices such as Tai Chi, Qi Gong, Acupressure, Acupuncture, Gua Sha, Herbal Medicine, Tui Na Massage and more.

paragraphs: Yang Practices:
Bali Yoga School offers a one-of-a-kind Yin Yoga Teacher Training Course where both Yin Yoga practice and Yang Yoga practice are a part of the curriculum during the course.
This thoughtfully curated course observes that understanding Yin becomes easier when students also understand its relationship with Yang.

The future Yin Yoga teacher needs to understand that different people will receive the practice differently, and it is important to experience Yin as a priority practice, not as a short course, to help students evolve from the idea of aesthetics attached to the asana practice. For this, one must take up the 500-hour Yin Yoga TTC course and help others transition.

sections.heading: Functional Anatomy, Fascia & Skeletal Variation: Why Every Body Experiences Yin Differently?
paragraphs: In Yang Practices, the mind is outward on the visibility of wearing the posture on the body. The idea of ideal posture and perfection dissolves and the habit to observe the posture inward develops gradually with the practice of Yin Yoga.

Explain that good Yin teaching should not be based on forcing every student into exactly the same shape. Yin Yoga emphasizes Safe-Positioning as you connect within the body with the fascia in the peak pose.

Two students can perform the same Yin posture correctly while looking completely different. A teacher therefore needs to understand whether a student’s limitation comes from muscular/tissue tension or from their individual skeletal structure and compression.

sections.heading: Yin-Yang Philosophy, Traditional Chinese Medicine & Meridian Theory
paragraphs: In the East, a steady observation of how the Sun and Moon support and influence life on earth gave rise to deep contemplation and development of natural philosophy and naturalism. Whether it is Ha-Tha (Yoga), Purusha – Prakriti (Samkhya), or Yin-Yang (Daoism), different schools of thought have long acknowledged the balance of these two vital forces.

Yin & Yang in Daoism are dual forces that complement each other and they are born from, or are the manifestation of, the vital life force called ‘chi’. In the Chinese traditions and belief systems the nature of duality has been widely studied to understand its effect on the body and on the mind. The Yin Yoga TTC at Bali Yoga School connects Yin Yoga with Yin-Yang philosophy and Traditional Chinese Medicine. It introduces stillness as a conscious choice beyond sleeping to manage productivity and resilience at the body and mind level. Taoist movements like Tai Chi and Qi Gong are replaced with Classical Hatha Yoga Asanas in Yin Yoga, but the philosophy of Stillness and Surrender in Daoism dominates the practice and makes it meditative.

Traditional Chinese Medicine believes that the Chi flows through energetic pathways called meridians, and excess or deficiency of any of the five elements – wood, metal, fire, water, earth – that correspond to each of the body organs causes subtle shifts in the flow of chi and, if not supported by the body, it causes blockages in the meridian pathways.

A Yin Yoga Teacher must understand that TCM & Daoism Philosophy is very important to explain physical illness, and equally important is anatomy to explain treatment through yin postures. A Yin teacher may use meridian-based themes when planning classes and conduct mindfulness and meditation practices from Daoism during long-held postures.

sections.heading: The Need to Build and Teach a Safe Yin Yoga Class
paragraphs: Deeper postures may give deeper injuries if practised unsupervised. The anatomical understanding of the teacher and knowledge of skeletal variations helps conduct a safe Yin Yoga class.
